publication.title: MLR-Bench: Evaluating AI Agents on Open-Ended Machine Learning Research

published_implementation.revision_relation: first-party implementation and result artifacts are present at the canonical review ref, but the paper does not bind every reported run to that exact Git commit

s4_path: generate a research idea from the assigned task
query recent external literature and synthesize relevant work/challenges with GPT-4o-Search-Preview
generate a prospective proposal/methodology/experimental design from task, idea and literature evidence
pass the proposal into the configured coding-agent experiment stage
execute experiments and return results into the research workspace and final paper

public_result_surfaces.literature_context: MLR-Agent uniformly uses GPT-4o-Search-Preview between idea generation and proposal generation to provide recent related-work reference material.
public_result_surfaces.interpretation: This evaluates a prospective S4-relevant output, but not the downstream benefit after the proposal is returned into experimentation. Cross-model variation also changes the model substrate rather than isolating a harness S4 mechanism.

The full canonical S4 path is present in the end-to-end organization, but the final-paper score mixes prospective adaptation with experimentation reliability, coding-agent behavior and paper writing, so it is not an isolated S4 capability result.

non_claim: The published proposal and end-to-end results are useful public evidence about MLR-Agent outputs, but they do not isolate the canonical S4 literature-to-proposal-to-later-operation relation. They are not a direct S4 observation, do not change S4=A ownership, and are not normalized into an S4 score.
